conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you during your stay. Can you tell me what brought you in today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I’ve been having way more diarrhea than usual—like 20 times yesterday. My normal is about 10, but this is out of control.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Any pain with that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, a lot. Left lower belly pain, sharp and crampy. Also some left flank pain that comes and goes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Is the flank pain like your kidney stones before?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Not really. My stones usually go to the middle, but this one stays on the left and goes down a bit.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that helps. I also see you mentioned black stools and a red tinge in your urine?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, saw that this morning. Worried me a bit.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll check that. Given your Crohn’s history, this sounds like a flare. Did anything change with your meds lately?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I dropped my prednisone to 5 mg last week. Felt weak, so I bumped it back to 10, then took 25 the day I came in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That could have triggered the flare. We’re going to start you on IV steroids to calm it down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Will that help the pain too?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It should, but we’ll also give you some IV Dilaudid for now to help with the discomfort.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks. I’ve been on prednisone for years—this is just how it goes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I know it’s tough. We’ll get you back on a higher dose and work with your GI doctor on long-term control.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your stool tests came back—no infection, no C. diff. That’s good news.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not something I caught?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, it looks like your Crohn’s acting up, not an infection. Your blood work is stable too—no kidney issues this time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about the blood in my urine? And the black stool?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Urine test showed no blood. Could’ve been old residue. The black stool worries me a bit—could be GI bleeding, but your hemoglobin is stable. We’ll watch it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Should we do a scope or something?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: GI doesn’t think it’s needed right now. Your symptoms point to a flare, and you’re already improving with steroids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did a renal ultrasound for your flank pain—kidneys look normal, no stones or blockage.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: But the pain’s still there. Could it be my back?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly. You have a history of disc disease. The pain moving around makes us think it’s musculoskeletal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It’s been worse today, shooting down my leg a bit.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll order an MRI of your lumbar spine to check if there’s new nerve pressure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your MRI is back. No new changes—same disc issues you’ve had. No nerve compression explaining the pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So why does it hurt so much?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hard to say. Sometimes chronic pain flares without a clear structural cause. We’ll keep managing it with meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m not making it up, if that’s what you’re thinking.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I believe you’re in pain. It’s just that scans don’t always show the full picture. We’ll keep treating it seriously.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re having fewer bowel movements—down to about 10. That’s great progress.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, feeling a bit better. Still tired.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re switching you from IV to oral prednisone—60 mg daily to control the flare.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I thought I was on 40 before?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, but we’re stepping up to get the inflammation under control, then we’ll taper slowly with your GI doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I just don’t want another flare soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll work on a plan. Also, you’re due for B12 shots—you haven’t had one in months?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know, but I keep forgetting. The clinic’s far.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your level is actually okay now, so we’ll just make sure you restart the shots regularly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your back pain is improving, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A little. Still there, but not as sharp.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We’ll switch your pain med to oral oxycodone for when you go home—just 10 pills, for breakthrough pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Only 10? What if it flares again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re being cautious. If it’s still bad, your primary can refill. But we want to avoid long-term opioid use.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I get it. I just want to function.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll also send you home with calcium and vitamin D. Long-term steroids weaken bones.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I can’t really afford those.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand, but they’re important. I’ll give you samples and a low-cost prescription. Your health comes first.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. We’re discharging you today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. What meds am I on now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Prednisone 40 mg daily, pantoprazole, calcium twice a day, vitamin D daily, and oxycodone as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the hospital bed?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ve arranged a semi-electric hospital bed for home. It’ll help you find a comfortable position.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks. When do I see GI?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Next week. They’ll adjust your prednisone and talk about other treatments to avoid future flares.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my back pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Follow up with your spine doctor. The MRI didn’t show new issues, so it’s likely part of your chronic pain pattern.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I’ll keep track of my symptoms.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good plan. Call us if diarrhea returns, or if you have fever, severe pain, or can’t keep fluids down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do. Thanks for everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and see you at your follow-up.
